claims.claim: Kir4.1 loss in satellite glial cells elicited a pronounced decrease in the levels of p-S6 and p-4-EBP1 in sympathetic neurons.
claims.source: Kir4.1 loss in satellite glial cells also elicited a pronounced decrease in the levels of p-S6 and p-4-EBP1, two well-established downstream effectors of mTOR activity (Meyuhas, 2008; Saxton and Sabatini, 2017), in sympathetic neurons (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), similar to the effects of satellite glia ablation (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by p-S6 and p-4-EBP1 immunostaining data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A. The characterization of p-S6 and p-4-EBP1 as mTOR effectors is supported by citations to Meyuhas, 2008 and Saxton and Sabatini, 2017.

claims.claim: There is an eightfold increase in apoptotic cells in Kir4.1 cKO sympathetic ganglia using TUNEL labeling at 14 days post-tamoxifen injection.
claims.source: Notably, we observed an eightfold increase in apoptotic cells in Kir4.1 cKO sympathetic ganglia using TUNEL labeling at 14 days post-tamoxifen injection (Figure 5D and E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by TUNEL labeling data shown in Figure 5D and E.

claims.claim: The apoptotic cells in Kir4.1 cKO sympathetic ganglia were primarily sympathetic neurons based on co-labeling for TUNEL and TrkA.
claims.source: The apoptotic cells were primarily sympathetic neurons based on co-labeling for TUNEL and TrkA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by TUNEL and TrkA co-labeling data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and C.

claims.claim: There was no increased apoptosis of satellite glial cells in Kir4.1 cKO sympathetic ganglia compared to controls.
claims.source: We did not observe increased apoptosis of satellite glial cells in Kir4.1 cKO sympathetic ganglia compared to controls (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D and E), consistent with results that the number of Sox2-positive satellite glia was not altered by Kir4.1 deletion (see Figure 4C and D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by TUNEL and Sox10 co-labeling data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D and E.

claims.claim: There is a 22% decrease in sympathetic neuron numbers in Kir4.1 cKO sympathetic ganglia by 2 weeks after tamoxifen injections.
claims.source: Consistent with enhanced neuronal apoptosis, we observed a 22% decrease in sympathetic neuron numbers in Kir4.1 cKO sympathetic ganglia by 2 weeks after tamoxifen injections (Figure 5F and G).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by Nissl staining and cell count data shown in Figure 5F and G.

claims.claim: Sympathetic axon innervation and axonal TH expression were similar between Kir4.1 cKO mice and controls.
claims.source: Similar to the findings in BLBP:iDTA mice, sympathetic axon innervation and axonal TH expression were similar between Kir4.1 cKO mice and controls (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F and G), despite the decrease in sympathetic neuron numbers and downregulated TH expression in neuronal cell bodies.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by TH immunostaining and quantification of innervation in salivary glands shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1F and G.

claims.claim: Kir4.1 is necessary for the survival of adult sympathetic neurons.
claims.source: Together, these results highlight that Kir4.1 is necessary for the survival of adult sympathetic neurons.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that Kir4.1 deletion in satellite glia results in increased neuronal apoptosis and decreased neuron numbers.

claims.claim: Basal pupil size, heart rate, and circulating NE levels were not significantly altered in Kir4.1 cKO mice.
claims.source: Measurements of basal pupil size, heart rate, and circulating NE levels indicated that these parameters were not significantly altered in Kir4.1 cKO mice (Figure 5H and I, Figure 5—figure supplement 1H–J), despite increased neuronal activity as assessed by c-Fos immunoreactivity (see Figure 4E and F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by pupil size measurements (Figure 5—figure supplement 1H–I), ECG recordings (Figure 5H and I), and NE ELISA data (Figure 5—figure supplement 1J).

claims.claim: Parasympathetic activity assessed by pupil constriction in response to different light intensities was normal in Kir4.1 cKO mice.
claims.source: Parasympathetic activity assessed by pupil constriction in response to different light intensities was also normal in Kir4.1 cKO mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 1K).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by pupil constriction measurements shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1K.

claims.claim: Kir4.1 deletion recapitulates the cellular phenotypes observed in BLBP:iDTA mice, notably, increased neuron activity, impaired metabolic signaling, and enhanced apoptosis.
claims.source: Together, these results suggest that Kir4.1 deletion recapitulates the cellular phenotypes observed in BLBP:iDTA mice, notably, increased neuron activity, impaired metabolic signaling, and enhanced apoptosis.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of phenotypes between Kir4.1 cKO and BLBP:iDTA mice.

claims.claim: The deletion of a single gene, Kcnj10 encoding for Kir4.1, from satellite glial cells is not sufficient to drive behavioral changes at the whole animal level as seen with genetic ablation of satellite glial cells.
claims.source: However, the deletion of a single gene, Kcnj10 encoding for Kir4.1, from satellite glial cells is not sufficient to drive behavioral changes at the whole animal level as seen with genetic ablation of satellite glial cells.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that Kir4.1 cKO mice do not show the autonomic behavioral defects (increased pupil size, heart rate, circulating NE) seen in BLBP:iDTA mice.

claims.claim: There are other satellite glia-dependent mechanisms, in addition to Kir4.1 activity, that contribute to regulation of neuronal excitability to drive circuit-level changes.
claims.source: These results suggest that there are other satellite glia-dependent mechanisms, in addition to Kir4.1 activity, that contribute to regulation of neuronal excitability to drive circuit-level changes.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that Kir4.1 deletion alone does not fully recapitulate the behavioral phenotypes of satellite glia ablation.

claims.claim: Satellite glia modulate sympathetic neuron metabolism, survival, neurotransmitter homeostasis, activity, and autonomic functions in adult mice.
claims.source: Here, we show that satellite glia modulate sympathetic neuron metabolism, survival, neurotransmitter homeostasis, activity, and autonomic functions in adult mice.
claims.evidence: This is a summary claim based on all the findings presented in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Neurons and their surrounding glial covers are functional units in the regulation of sympathetic output.
claims.source: Together, our findings provide in vivo evidence that neurons and their surrounding glial covers are functional units in the regulation of sympathetic output.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the collective findings that satellite glia regulate multiple aspects of sympathetic neuron function and autonomic behaviors.

claims.claim: A key role for satellite glia is in restraining neuronal activity in mature sympathetic neurons.
claims.source: We reveal that a key role for satellite glia is in restraining neuronal activity in mature sympathetic neurons.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that satellite glia depletion results in increased neuronal activity (c-Fos expression) and elevated sympathetic tone.

claims.claim: Depletion of satellite glia in adult mice amplifies neuronal activity, leading to increased circulating levels of NE and elevated sympathetic tone.
claims.source: Depletion of satellite glia in adult mice amplifies neuronal activity, leading to increased circulating levels of NE and elevated sympathetic tone.
claims.evidence: This is supported by data showing increased c-Fos expression, elevated circulating NE, increased pupil size, and elevated heart rate in BLBP:iDTA mice.

claims.claim: Glia-ablated mice show enhanced pupil size and heart rate, demonstrating the necessity of these cells in the dynamic regulation of autonomic functions in conscious and freely moving animals.
claims.source: Glia-ablated mice show enhanced pupil size and heart rate, demonstrating the necessity of these cells in the dynamic regulation of autonomic functions in conscious and freely moving animals.
claims.evidence: This is supported by pupil size and ECG data from BLBP:iDTA mice.

claims.claim: Satellite glia limit neuronal activity, similar to reported functions of other glial cells that encapsulate neuronal cell bodies, in particular, astrocytes, microglia, and cortex glia in Drosophila.
claims.source: Our findings that satellite glia limit neuronal activity are similar to reported functions of other glial cells that encapsulate neuronal cell bodies, in particular, astrocytes (Allen and Lyons, 2018), microglia (Badimon et al., 2020; Cserép et al., 2020), and cortex glia in Drosophila (Yadav et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is a comparison to published literature supported by citations to Allen and Lyons, 2018; Badimon et al., 2020; Cserép et al., 2020; and Yadav et al., 2019.

claims.claim: Inhibitory effects of satellite glia might enable sympathetic neurons to respond to a wider range of input strengths and/or serve as a neuroprotective mechanism to limit neurotoxicity under conditions of stress or pathology.
claims.source: Inhibitory effects of satellite glia might enable sympathetic neurons to respond to a wider range of input strengths and/or serve as a neuroprotective mechanism to limit neurotoxicity under conditions of stress or pathology.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential functional implications of satellite glia's inhibitory effects.

claims.claim: Glial regulation of ion homeostasis, specifically K+ clearance, is a key mechanism that contributes to inhibition of neuronal activity.
claims.source: The enhanced neuronal c-Fos signals in Kir4.1 cKO and satellite glia-ablated mice suggest that glial regulation of ion homeostasis, specifically, K+ clearance, is a key mechanism that contributes to inhibition of neuronal activity.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that both satellite glia ablation and Kir4.1 deletion result in increased neuronal activity.

claims.claim: Satellite glia have high K+ conductance, which is almost exclusively dependent on Kir4.1 expression.
claims.source: Electrophysiological analyses show that satellite glia have high K+ conductance, which is almost exclusively dependent on Kir4.1 expression (Tang et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Tang et al., 2010.

claims.claim: Satellite glial cells are coupled to one another through gap junctions.
claims.source: Satellite glial cells are also coupled to one another through gap junctions (Huang et al., 2005; Kim et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Huang et al., 2005 and Kim et al., 2016.

claims.claim: RNAi-mediated knockdown of Kir4.1 or Connexin 43 enhances excitability of sensory neurons and evokes nociceptive responses in rats.
claims.source: RNAi-mediated knockdown of Kir4.1 or Connexin 43, a gap junction protein, enhances excitability of sensory neurons and evokes nociceptive responses in rats (Ohara et al., 2008; Vit et al., 2008; Ohara et al., 2008; Vit et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ohara et al., 2008 and Vit et al., 2008.

claims.claim: Satellite glia are capable of taking up extracellular K+, distributing them throughout a glial syncytium via gap junction coupling, and extruding ions in regions of low K+ concentration, in a process called 'spatial K+ buffering'.
claims.source: Together, these studies suggest that satellite glia are capable of taking up extracellular K+, distributing them throughout a glial syncytium via gap junction coupling, and extruding ions in regions of low K+ concentration, in a process called 'spatial K+ buffering' (Kuffler, 1967; Tang et al., 2010), similar to astrocyte functions in the CNS (Kofuji and Newman, 2004).
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference based on published literature, supported by citations to Kuffler, 1967; Tang et al., 2010; and Kofuji and Newman, 2004.

claims.claim: Even slight elevations in extracellular K+ in the neuronal microenvironment, due to loss of glial Kir4.1, are likely to elicit neuronal depolarization and activation.
claims.source: Even slight elevations in extracellular K+ in the neuronal microenvironment, due to loss of glial Kir4.1, are likely to elicit neuronal depolarization and activation (Cui et al., 2018; Haydon, 2001).
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference supported by citations to Cui et al., 2018 and Haydon, 2001.

claims.claim: Kir4.1 is a major contributor to the hyperpolarized resting membrane potential of satellite glia.
claims.source: For example, Kir4.1 is a major contributor to the hyperpolarized resting membrane potential of satellite glia (Tang et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Tang et al., 2010.

claims.claim: Depolarization of satellite glia, induced by loss of Kir4.1, could likely affect voltage-dependent processes in these cells.
claims.source: Depolarization of satellite glia, induced by loss of Kir4.1, could likely affect voltage-dependent processes in these cells (Tang et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential mechanisms, supported by citation to Tang et al., 2010.

claims.claim: Kir4.1, expressed in astrocytes, inhibits the synthesis of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) in astrocytes.
claims.source: Kir4.1, expressed in astrocytes, inhibits the synthesis of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) in astrocytes (Kinboshi et al., 2017; Ohno et al., 2018), and astrocyte-derived BDNF has been shown to enhance neuronal activity through presynaptic mechanisms in the ventromedial hypothalamus (Ameroso et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kinboshi et al., 2017; Ohno et al., 2018; and Ameroso et al., 2022.

claims.claim: An analogous Kir4.1-BDNF pathway might operate in satellite glia to influence neuron activity since BDNF is known to increase presynaptic input to post-ganglionic sympathetic neurons in sympathetic ganglia.
claims.source: Thus, an analogous Kir4.1-BDNF pathway might operate in satellite glia to influence neuron activity since BDNF is known to increase presynaptic input to post-ganglionic sympathetic neurons in sympathetic ganglia (Causing et al., 1997).
claims.evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential mechanisms in satellite glia, with the BDNF effect in sympathetic ganglia supported by citation to Causing et al., 1997.

claims.claim: Satellite glia-specific loss of Kir4.1 recapitulates all the cellular phenotypes observed in BLBP:iDTA sympathetic neurons, specifically, increased neuronal activity, diminished mTOR signaling, soma atrophy, downregulated expression of noradrenergic enzymes, and neuronal apoptosis.
claims.source: We found that satellite glia-specific loss of Kir4.1 recapitulates all the cellular phenotypes observed in BLBP:iDTA sympathetic neurons, specifically, increased neuronal activity, diminished mTOR signaling, soma atrophy, downregulated expression of noradrenergic enzymes, and neuronal apoptosis.
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement based on comparison of phenotypes between Kir4.1 cKO and BLBP:iDTA mice.

claims.claim: Additional glia-dependent mechanisms must contribute to neuronal excitability to drive network-level changes beyond Kir4.1.
claims.source: Thus, additional glia-dependent mechanisms must contribute to neuronal excitability to drive network-level changes.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that Kir4.1 deletion does not fully recapitulate the behavioral phenotypes of satellite glia ablation.

claims.claim: Satellite glia could influence neuronal activity via regulation of ganglionic levels of acetylcholine, the major neurotransmitter released by pre-ganglionic axons.
claims.source: Satellite glia could influence neuronal activity via regulation of ganglionic levels of acetylcholine, the major neurotransmitter released by pre-ganglionic axons.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential mechanisms.

claims.claim: Satellite glia modulate cholinergic neurotransmission in co-cultured sympathetic neurons.
claims.source: Despite previous observations that satellite glia modulate cholinergic neurotransmission in co-cultured sympathetic neurons (Enes et al., 2020; Feldman-Goriachnik et al., 2018), we did not detect glial transcripts involved in cholinergic signaling using single-cell RNA-sequencing of sympathetic ganglia (Mapps et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: The claim about modulation in co-culture is supported by citations to Enes et al., 2020 and Feldman-Goriachnik et al., 2018. The lack of detection in single-cell RNA-seq is supported by citation to Mapps et al., 2022.

claims.claim: Another potential mechanism could involve glial regulation of extracellular ATP and/or its breakdown products in the neuronal microenvironment.
claims.source: Another potential mechanism could involve glial regulation of extracellular ATP and/or its breakdown products in the neuronal microenvironment (Hanani, 2010).
claims.evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential mechanisms, with general context supported by citation to Hanani, 2010.

claims.claim: In sympathetic ganglia, ATP is largely released by innervating cholinergic pre-ganglionic axons and facilitates fast excitatory neurotransmission in post-ganglionic sympathetic neurons.
claims.source: In sympathetic ganglia, ATP is largely released by innervating cholinergic pre-ganglionic axons and facilitates fast excitatory neurotransmission in post-ganglionic sympathetic neurons (Boehm, 1999; Evans et al., 1992; McCaman and McAfee, 1986; Vizi et al., 1997).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Boehm, 1999; Evans et al., 1992; McCaman and McAfee, 1986; and Vizi et al., 1997.

claims.claim: Extracellular ATP is rapidly metabolized by cell-surface ectonucleotidases, which are expressed in sympathetic satellite glia.
claims.source: Extracellular ATP is rapidly metabolized by cell-surface ectonucleotidases, which are expressed in sympathetic satellite glia (Forsman and Elfvin, 1984; Nacimiento et al., 1991; Vizi et al., 1997).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Forsman and Elfvin, 1984; Nacimiento et al., 1991; and Vizi et al., 1997.

claims.claim: Single-cell RNA-sequencing data revealed several transcripts involved in ATP sensing, hydrolysis, and removal of breakdown products in sympathetic satellite glia, including P2rx4, P2rx7, P2ry12, Entpd1, and Adk.
claims.source: Single-cell RNA-sequencing data revealed several transcripts involved in ATP sensing, hydrolysis, and removal of breakdown products in sympathetic satellite glia, including the purinergic receptors, P2rx4, P2rx7, and P2ry12, and Entpd1, an ectoenzyme which catalyzes ATP to ADP hydrolysis, as well as Adk (adenosine kinase) (Mapps et al., 2022), which is best known for mediating astrocytic uptake of extracellular adenosine in the brain (Boison et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell RNA-sequencing data from Mapps et al., 2022. The function of Adk in astrocytes is supported by citation to Boison et al., 2010.

claims.claim: Autonomic defects observed in BLBP:iDTA mice arise primarily from defects in peripheral sympathetic neurons.
claims.source: Our results suggest that autonomic defects observed in BLBP:iDTA mice arise primarily from defects in peripheral sympathetic neurons.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the 6-OHDA rescue experiment and other control experiments.

claims.claim: 6-OHDA-mediated ablation of sympathetic nerves prevents elevated heart rate in BLBP:iDTA mice.
claims.source: We demonstrate that 6-OHDA-mediated ablation of sympathetic nerves prevents elevated heart rate in BLBP:iDTA mice.
claims.evidence: This is supported by ECG data after 6-OHDA treatment shown in Figure 3E and F.

claims.claim: Since 6-OHDA selectively destroys sympathetic nerves, these results exclude the involvement of sensory or parasympathetic neurons to the cardiac defect in BLBP:iDTA mice.
claims.source: Since 6-OHDA selectively destroys sympathetic nerves (Kostrzewa and Jacobowitz, 1974), these results exclude the involvement of sensory or parasympathetic neurons to the cardiac defect in BLBP:iDTA mice.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the 6-OHDA rescue experiment and the known selectivity of 6-OHDA (supported by citation to Kostrzewa and Jacobowitz, 1974).

claims.claim: Parasympathetic function in BLBP:iDTA mice appears to be unaffected since mutant mice fully constrict their pupils in response to light.
claims.source: Parasympathetic function in BLBP:iDTA mice appears to be unaffected since mutant mice fully constrict their pupils in response to light.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the pupil constriction data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: BLBP is expressed in neuronal progenitors, radial glia, and astrocytes in the CNS.
claims.source: BLBP is also expressed in neuronal progenitors, radial glia, and astrocytes in the CNS (Ebrahimi et al., 2016; Feng et al., 1994; Matsumata et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ebrahimi et al., 2016; Feng et al., 1994; and Matsumata et al., 2012.

claims.claim: Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis indicates an approximately 45-fold enrichment of Fabp7 transcript in satellite glia relative to astrocytes.
claims.source: Our single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis of satellite glia (Mapps et al., 2022) compared to published single-cell RNA studies of astrocytes (Batiuk et al., 2020) indicates an ~45-fold enrichment of Fabp7 transcript in satellite glia relative to astrocytes.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on comparison of single-cell RNA-seq data from Mapps et al., 2022 and Batiuk et al., 2020.

claims.claim: Astrocyte ablation in adult mice results in severe motor deficits, including limb paralysis, ataxia, as well as smaller body weight.
claims.source: Further, astrocyte ablation in adult mice results in severe motor deficits, including limb paralysis, ataxia, as well as smaller body weight (Schreiner et al., 2015), none of which were observed in BLBP:iDTA mice.
claims.evidence: The claim about astrocyte ablation phenotypes is supported by citation to Schreiner et al., 2015. The lack of these phenotypes in BLBP:iDTA mice is an observation from the current study.

claims.claim: Astrocyte-specific deletion of Kcnj10 using GFAP-cre mice results in premature lethality, epileptic seizures, and severe ataxia.
claims.source: Similarly, astrocyte-specific deletion of Kcnj10 using GFAP-cre mice results in premature lethality, epileptic seizures, and severe ataxia (Djukic et al., 2007), none of which were observed with Kir4.1 deletion using Fabp7-CreER2 mice.
claims.evidence: The claim about astrocyte-specific Kcnj10 deletion phenotypes is supported by citation to Djukic et al., 2007. The lack of these phenotypes in Kir4.1 cKO mice is an observation from the current study.

claims.claim: Astrocytes are minimally perturbed in BLBP:iDTA and Kir4.1 cKO mice.
claims.source: Together, these results suggest that astrocytes are minimally perturbed in BLBP:iDTA and Kir4.1 cKO mice.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of CNS phenotypes typically associated with astrocyte dysfunction.

claims.claim: Chemogenetic manipulation of satellite glia by activating a Gq-GPCR signaling pathway increased heart rate in Gfap-hM3Dq mice.
claims.source: In a previous study, chemogenetic manipulation of satellite glia by activating a Gq-GPCR signaling pathway increased heart rate in Gfap-hM3Dq mice (Xie et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Xie et al., 2017.

claims.claim: Sympathetic satellite glia, very likely, exert both excitatory and inhibitory effects on neuronal activity in a context-dependent manner, similar to astrocyte functions in the brain.
claims.source: Nevertheless, sympathetic satellite glia, very likely, exert both excitatory and inhibitory effects on neuronal activity in a context-dependent manner, similar to astrocyte functions in the brain (Allen and Lyons, 2018).
claims.evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential dual functions of satellite glia, with comparison to astrocytes supported by citation to Allen and Lyons, 2018.

claims.claim: Under conditions of nerve injury or inflammation, activated sensory satellite glia are known to undergo structural and functional changes, resulting in neuronal hyper-excitability.
claims.source: Specifically, under conditions of nerve injury or inflammation, activated sensory satellite glia are known to undergo structural and functional changes, resulting in neuronal hyper-excitability (Hanani and Spray, 2020).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Hanani and Spray, 2020.

claims.claim: In response to nerve damage, sympathetic satellite glia are capable of reactive changes, specifically, enhanced gap junction-mediated coupling and increased ATP sensitivity.
claims.source: Limited studies, so far, suggest that in response to nerve damage, sympathetic satellite glia are also capable of reactive changes, specifically, enhanced gap junction-mediated coupling and increased ATP sensitivity (Feldman-Goriachnik and Hanani, 2019), which, in turn, may augment neuronal activity.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Feldman-Goriachnik and Hanani, 2019.

claims.claim: Satellite glia depletion or glial deletion of Kir4.1 resulted in the loss of approximately 25% of adult sympathetic neurons.
claims.source: An intriguing finding was that satellite glia depletion or glial deletion of Kir4.1 resulted in the loss of ~25% of adult sympathetic neurons.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the neuronal loss data from BLBP:iDTA (24% decrease) and Kir4.1 cKO (22% decrease) mice.

claims.claim: The exquisite dependence of sympathetic neurons on the target-derived survival factor, nerve growth factor (NGF), during development is well-documented.
claims.source: The exquisite dependence of sympathetic neurons on the target-derived survival factor, nerve growth factor (NGF), during development is well-documented (Glebova and Ginty, 2005).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Glebova and Ginty, 2005.

claims.claim: Loss of NGF signaling does not compromise the survival of adult sympathetic neurons.
claims.source: However, loss of NGF signaling does not compromise the survival of adult neurons (Angeletti et al., 1971; Tsui-Pierchala and Ginty, 1999), and to date, the trophic mechanisms underlying adult sympathetic neuron survival in vivo remain undefined.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Angeletti et al., 1971 and Tsui-Pierchala and Ginty, 1999.

claims.claim: The similar phenotypes of soma atrophy, impaired mTOR signaling, and enhanced apoptosis in adult BLBP:iDTA and Kir4.1 cKO sympathetic neurons suggest that satellite glia provide metabolic and trophic support to mature neurons, primarily, via regulation of K+ homeostasis.
claims.source: The similar phenotypes of soma atrophy, impaired mTOR signaling, and enhanced apoptosis in adult BLBP:iDTA and Kir4.1 cKO sympathetic neurons suggest that satellite glia provide metabolic and trophic support to mature neurons, primarily, via regulation of K+ homeostasis.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of phenotypes between BLBP:iDTA and Kir4.1 cKO mice.

claims.claim: Astrocyte-specific Kir4.1 deletion results in defects in mTOR signaling and decreased soma size, but not cell death, in a population of spinal cord motor neurons.
claims.source: Of note, astrocyte-specific Kir4.1 deletion also results in defects in mTOR signaling and decreased soma size, but not cell death, in a population of spinal cord motor neurons (Kelley et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Kelley et al., 2018.

claims.claim: Despite enhanced sympathetic neuron activity and circulating NE levels in satellite glia-ablated mice, there is a pronounced downregulation of NE biosynthetic machinery, specifically in neuronal cell bodies.
claims.source: Further, despite enhanced sympathetic neuron activity and circulating NE levels in satellite glia-ablated mice, we observed a pronounced downregulation of NE biosynthetic machinery, specifically in neuronal cell bodies.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of observations from the manuscript showing downregulated TH and DBH in soma despite elevated NE and activity.

claims.claim: The downregulation of NE biosynthetic machinery in neuronal cell bodies may reflect a compensatory response to elevated sympathetic activity upon glia loss or the need for glia-derived factors in maintenance of noradrenergic enzymes.
claims.source: This may reflect a compensatory response to elevated sympathetic activity upon glia loss or the need for glia-derived factors in maintenance of noradrenergic enzymes.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential mechanisms underlying the downregulation of NE biosynthetic enzymes.

claims.claim: Satellite glia depletion resulted in soma-specific effects in sympathetic neurons, that is, TH downregulation and soma size decrease, without perturbing axonal TH levels and innervation.
claims.source: It is also notable that satellite glia depletion resulted in soma-specific effects in sympathetic neurons, that is, TH downregulation and soma size decrease, without perturbing axonal TH levels and innervation.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of observations comparing somatic versus axonal phenotypes in BLBP:iDTA mice.

claims.claim: Th mRNA is trafficked to sympathetic axons, where it is locally translated.
claims.source: Th mRNA is trafficked to sympathetic axons, where it is locally translated (Gervasi et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Gervasi et al., 2016.

claims.claim: Enhanced Th mRNA trafficking and local synthesis might be a mechanism to maintain axonal TH expression and to locally regulate NE release in BLBP:iDTA sympathetic neurons.
claims.source: Thus, enhanced Th mRNA trafficking and local synthesis might be a mechanism to maintain axonal TH expression and to locally regulate NE release in BLBP:iDTA sympathetic neurons.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential mechanisms to maintain axonal TH despite somatic downregulation.

claims.claim: Heightened activity of the sympathetic nervous system is a characteristic feature of several pathological conditions, specifically, chronic heart failure, arrhythmias, hypertension, sleep apnea, obesity, and insulin resistance.
claims.source: Heightened activity of the sympathetic nervous system is a characteristic feature of several pathological conditions, specifically, chronic heart failure (Malpas, 2010), arrhythmias (Hasan, 2013; Schwartz, 2014), hypertension (Goldstein et al., 2002; Schlaich et al., 2004), sleep apnea, obesity, and insulin resistance (Mahfoud et al., 2011; Mancia et al., 2007; Schlaich et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Malpas, 2010; Hasan, 2013; Schwartz, 2014; Goldstein et al., 2002; Schlaich et al., 2004; Mahfoud et al., 2011; and Mancia et al., 2007.

claims.claim: This study highlights the therapeutic potential of targeting the neuron–satellite glia unit in autonomic-related diseases.
claims.source: While sympathetic neurons, so far, have been at the center stage in considering pathological mechanisms and treatments, our study, together with other recent work (Xie et al., 2017), highlights the therapeutic potential of targeting the neuron–satellite glia unit in autonomic-related diseases.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential therapeutic implications, with reference to another study (Xie et al., 2017).

claims.claim: Satellite glia are the major glial cells in sympathetic ganglia, enveloping neuronal cell bodies.
claims.source: Satellite glia are the major glial cells in sympathetic ganglia (Hanani, 2010; Mapps et al., 2021) and have a unique architecture in completely enveloping neuronal cell bodies (Elfvin and Forsman, 1978; Gabella et al., 1988).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hanani, 2010; Mapps et al., 2021; Elfvin and Forsman, 1978; and Gabella et al., 1988.

claims.claim: Each neuron and associated glia are thought to form a discrete structural and functional unit.
claims.source: Each neuron and associated glia are thought to form a discrete structural and functional unit (Hanani, 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Hanani, 2010.

claims.claim: Satellite glial cells are derived from multipotent neural crest precursors.
claims.source: Like neurons, satellite glial cells are derived from multipotent neural crest precursors and form thin cytoplasmic sheaths around cell bodies, dendrites, and synapses of sympathetic neurons, with only 20 nm of space, the width of a synaptic cleft, between neuronal and glial membranes (Elfvin and Forsman, 1978; Gabella et al., 1988; Hanani, 2010; Pannese, 1981).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Elfvin and Forsman, 1978; Gabella et al., 1988; Hanani, 2010; and Pannese, 1981.

claims.claim: Multiple satellite glia surround a single neuron and are connected with each other, and with neurons, via gap junctions, with the number of glial cells per neuron being positively correlated to soma size.
claims.source: Multiple satellite glia surround a single neuron and are connected with each other, and with neurons, via gap junctions, with the number of glial cells per neuron being positively correlated to soma size (Elfvin and Forsman, 1978; Hanani, 2010; Ledda et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Elfvin and Forsman, 1978; Hanani, 2010; and Ledda et al., 2004.

claims.claim: Studies in sympathetic neuron–glia co-cultures have suggested roles for satellite glia in promoting dendrite growth, synapse formation, modulating extracellular ion and neurotransmitter concentrations, and regulating synaptic transmission.
claims.source: Studies in sympathetic neuron–glia co-cultures have suggested roles for satellite glia in promoting dendrite growth, synapse formation, modulating extracellular ion and neurotransmitter concentrations, and regulating synaptic transmission (Enes et al., 2020; Feldman-Goriachnik et al., 2018; Hanani, 2010; Tropea et al., 1988).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Enes et al., 2020; Feldman-Goriachnik et al., 2018; Hanani, 2010; and Tropea et al., 1988.

claims.claim: Recent studies implicate sensory satellite glia in regulating chronic pain through modulating neuronal hyper-excitability.
claims.source: Recent studies implicate sensory satellite glia in regulating chronic pain through modulating neuronal hyper-excitability (Kim et al., 2016), and in promoting axon regeneration after peripheral nerve injury in vivo (Avraham et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2016 and Avraham et al., 2020.

claims.claim: Satellite glia have been proposed to be closest to astrocytes in the central nervous system (CNS) with respect to expression of machinery related to neurotransmitter uptake/turnover, inward-rectifying potassium channels, functional coupling via gap junctions, and close association with synapses.
claims.source: Satellite glia have been proposed to be closest to astrocytes in the central nervous system (CNS) with respect to expression of machinery related to neurotransmitter uptake/turnover, inward-rectifying potassium channels, functional coupling via gap junctions, and close association with synapses (Hanani and Spray, 2020; Hanani and Verkhratsky, 2021).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hanani and Spray, 2020 and Hanani and Verkhratsky, 2021.

results.result: BLBP (Fabp7) is specifically enriched in satellite glia of adult mouse sympathetic ganglia, and Fabp7-CreER2 mice enable satellite glia-specific genetic manipulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C3 demonstrate BLBP enrichment via single-cell RNA-seq (140-fold), developmental expression patterns, and reporter mouse specificity with multiple cell-type markers. The convergent evidence from transcriptomics, immunostaining, and genetic reporters strongly supports satellite glia specificity.

results.result: Tamoxifen-induced DTA expression in BLBP:iDTA mice causes progressive satellite glia apoptosis and loss without compensatory proliferation or macrophage infiltration.
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C13 provide temporal analysis showing glial apoptosis at 5 dpi (C4-C6) and substantial loss by 14 dpi (C7-C10), with appropriate controls for inflammation and proliferation (C11-C13). Multiple quantification methods (TUNEL, Sox2, binary imaging, qPCR) converge on consistent findings.

results.result: Satellite glia depletion causes downregulation of noradrenergic biosynthetic enzymes (TH and DBH), neuronal soma atrophy, and impaired mTOR signaling in sympathetic neurons.
results.evaluation: Claims C14-C19 demonstrate dramatic reductions in TH (88%) and DBH (99%) transcripts, reduced soma size (median 162 vs 118 μm²), and decreased mTOR effectors (p-S6, p-4-EBP1). The mechanistic link between mTOR and soma size is well-established, supporting the inference in C19.

results.result: Satellite glia depletion leads to delayed neuronal loss (24% by 14 dpi) while maintaining axonal innervation and differential TH regulation in soma versus axons.
results.evaluation: Claims C20-C24 show no neuronal loss at 5 dpi but significant loss by 14 dpi, with preserved axonal innervation and TH levels in axons despite somatic downregulation. The temporal progression and compartment-specific effects are well-documented, though the mechanism for differential TH regulation (C23) requires further investigation.

results.result: BLBP:iDTA mice exhibit increased basal pupil size and elevated heart rate with intact parasympathetic function, indicating elevated sympathetic tone.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C31 demonstrate increased pupil size and heart rate with normal pupil constriction responses to light, supported by appropriate tamoxifen controls. The inference of elevated sympathetic tone (C28) is well-supported by the pattern of autonomic measurements.

results.result: 6-OHDA-mediated ablation of peripheral sympathetic nerves rescues the elevated heart rate in BLBP:iDTA mice, confirming peripheral sympathetic neuron dysfunction as the primary cause.
results.evaluation: Claims C32-C34, C89-C90 provide a critical rescue experiment demonstrating that selective sympathetic nerve ablation prevents cardiac phenotypes. The specificity of 6-OHDA for sympathetic nerves and peripheral restriction is well-established in cited literature, making this a strong mechanistic validation.

results.result: Satellite glia depletion results in elevated circulating norepinephrine, compensatory downregulation of cardiac adrenergic receptors, and increased neuronal c-Fos expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C38 demonstrate 1.6-fold increased NE, decreased cardiac adrenergic receptor expression, and 8-fold increased c-Fos+ neurons. The pattern is internally consistent with elevated sympathetic activity and compensatory receptor downregulation, though the paradox of increased NE despite reduced biosynthetic enzymes requires mechanistic explanation.

results.result: Kir4.1 is enriched in satellite glia and can be specifically deleted using Fabp7-CreER2 mice without affecting glial numbers or morphology.
results.evaluation: Claims C39-C45 establish Kir4.1 expression (3-fold enrichment), successful deletion (76% reduction), and preservation of glial numbers and morphology. Multiple validation methods (RNA-seq, qPCR, smFISH, immunostaining) provide robust evidence for the conditional knockout model.

results.result: Satellite glia-specific Kir4.1 deletion increases neuronal c-Fos expression and downregulates noradrenergic enzymes, similar to satellite glia ablation.
results.evaluation: Claims C46-C49 show increased c-Fos+ cells (primarily neurons) and reduced TH/DBH expression in Kir4.1 cKO mice, recapitulating key cellular phenotypes from BLBP:iDTA mice. This convergence from two independent genetic models strengthens the mechanistic role of Kir4.1.

results.result: Kir4.1 deletion in satellite glia causes neuronal soma atrophy, impaired mTOR signaling, increased neuronal apoptosis (8-fold), and 22% neuronal loss while preserving axonal innervation.
results.evaluation: Claims C51-C57 demonstrate that Kir4.1 deletion recapitulates the cellular phenotypes of satellite glia ablation, including reduced soma size, decreased mTOR effectors, and neuronal loss. The specificity for neuronal (not glial) apoptosis (C53-C54) is well-documented with appropriate markers.

results.result: Kir4.1 deletion recapitulates cellular but not behavioral phenotypes of satellite glia ablation, indicating additional glia-dependent mechanisms regulate autonomic function.
results.evaluation: Claims C58-C62 show that despite cellular similarities, Kir4.1 cKO mice lack the autonomic behavioral defects (pupil size, heart rate, circulating NE) seen in BLBP:iDTA mice. This important negative result is well-controlled and suggests Kir4.1-independent mechanisms contribute to circuit-level regulation.

results.result: Satellite glia modulate multiple aspects of sympathetic neuron function and restrain neuronal activity to regulate autonomic output in vivo.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C67 synthesize the major findings into an overarching conclusion about satellite glia function. The evidence from genetic ablation, cellular phenotypes, and behavioral measurements provides strong support for this integrative conclusion about neuron-glia functional units.

results.result: Satellite glia likely inhibit neuronal activity through Kir4.1-dependent K+ buffering, similar to astrocyte functions in the CNS.
results.evaluation: Claims C68-C75 propose K+ homeostasis as a key mechanism based on increased c-Fos in both ablation and Kir4.1 deletion models, supported by extensive literature on Kir4.1 function and spatial K+ buffering. The mechanistic inference is well-grounded in established glial physiology.

results.result: Additional mechanisms beyond K+ buffering, including potential BDNF signaling, cholinergic modulation, and ATP metabolism, may contribute to satellite glia regulation of neuronal excitability.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C87 propose multiple alternative or complementary mechanisms, but most are speculative (C77, C79, C82, C84) or based solely on literature (C78, C83, C85-C86). While C87 provides RNA-seq evidence for ATP-related transcripts, functional validation is lacking. These hypotheses require experimental testing.

results.result: The autonomic phenotypes in BLBP:iDTA mice arise from peripheral sympathetic neurons rather than CNS astrocyte dysfunction.
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C96 address the critical specificity concern about BLBP expression in CNS glia. The 6-OHDA rescue (C89), normal parasympathetic function (C91), 45-fold enrichment in satellite glia vs astrocytes (C93), and absence of CNS phenotypes (C94-C95) provide convergent evidence for peripheral localization, though complete exclusion of CNS contribution is difficult.

results.result: Satellite glia may exert context-dependent excitatory and inhibitory effects on neurons, with reactive changes under pathological conditions.
results.evaluation: Claims C97-C100 discuss potential dual functions of satellite glia based on literature, but the comparison to chemogenetic activation (C97) involves different experimental paradigms. The speculation about context-dependent effects (C98) and reactive changes (C99-C100) is reasonable but requires direct experimental validation in the current model system.

results.result: Satellite glia provide metabolic and trophic support for adult sympathetic neuron survival primarily through K+ homeostasis, independent of NGF signaling.
results.evaluation: Claims C101-C105 establish that ~25% of adult sympathetic neurons require satellite glia for survival, with similar phenotypes in both genetic models suggesting K+-dependent mechanisms. The comparison to NGF independence (C102-C103) and astrocyte-specific Kir4.1 deletion (C105) provides important context, though the exact trophic mechanisms remain undefined.

results.result: Satellite glia depletion causes compartment-specific effects with downregulated TH in soma but maintained axonal TH, potentially through enhanced local mRNA trafficking and translation.
results.evaluation: Claims C106-C110 document an intriguing soma-axon differential in TH regulation. While the observation is well-supported (C106, C108), the proposed mechanism of enhanced Th mRNA trafficking (C110) is speculative. The paradox of reduced somatic TH but increased circulating NE (C106) requires mechanistic resolution.

results.result: This study highlights therapeutic potential for targeting the neuron-satellite glia unit in autonomic-related diseases characterized by sympathetic hyperactivity.
results.evaluation: Claims C111-C112 propose translational implications based on the association between sympathetic hyperactivity and various pathologies (C111). While the basic science findings are robust, the therapeutic potential (C112) is speculative and would require validation in disease models and assessment of whether satellite glia dysfunction contributes to these conditions.

results.result: Satellite glia are specialized glial cells that form discrete structural and functional units with neurons in sympathetic ganglia, sharing features with CNS astrocytes.
results.evaluation: Claims C113-C119 provide established background on satellite glia architecture and function, well-supported by extensive literature citations. These contextual claims establish the rationale for the study and are appropriately referenced to prior work.
